title: New Year 2027 Around the World: Who Celebrates First?
summary: Discover who celebrates New Year 2027 first and last, why time zones matter, and how to plan calls or messages to loved ones worldwide. Stay connected this New Year!
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Kiribati is the first country to ring in 2027, starting with Kiritimati and the rest of its Line Islands. When it’s midnight there on January 1, 2027, it’s still December 31 in the US: 5 a.m. in New York and 2 a.m. in Los Angeles. New Zealand’s Chatham Islands follow 15 minutes later, and Auckland and Wellington celebrate 45 minutes after that.*


**If you’ve ever wondered who gets to say “Happy New Year” first, the answer starts in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. Thanks to the way the world’s time zones are drawn, some places step into January 1 while people across the US are still finishing their December 31 breakfast. Knowing the order—and the exact times—makes it easier to send a timely text, plan a video call, or simply understand why your friend in Auckland is already toasting 2027 while you’re still wrapping up work.**


**This guide walks through which places celebrate first, why Kiribati beats New Zealand to the punch, and which spots on Earth are the very last to leave 2026 behind. Along the way, you’ll find a time zone table you can use to look up dozens of cities in both Eastern Time (ET) and Pacific Time (PT)—useful if you’re hoping to call a loved one the moment their clock strikes midnight.**


## What order do countries celebrate New Year 2027?


Here’s a practical example: if you want to text family in Manila the moment their calendar flips to January 1, send your message at 11 a.m. ET or 8 a.m. PT on December 31.


That’s because Manila sits many hours ahead of the US on the clock, even though both places are experiencing the same moment in time. UTC, or Coordinated Universal Time, is the reference point the world uses to compare these differences—you’ll see it throughout this guide as a shorthand for how far ahead or behind a location is.


The table below groups cities and countries by[when they hit midnight on January 1, 2027](https://timecrisp.com/new-year/) , using representative cities for countries that span multiple time zones. Each row also shows the equivalent time in US Eastern and Pacific zones, so you can find the right moment to say hello.

For more cities or to switch the schedule to your own time zone, check t[imeanddate.com’s full worldwide New Year 2027 countdown](https://www.timeanddate.com/countdown/newyear) .*


## Why does Kiribati celebrate before New Zealand?


The short answer lies in the International Date Line, an imaginary boundary that separates one calendar date from the next.[According to NOAA’s National Ocean Service](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/international-date-line.html) , this line doesn’t run in a perfectly straight path—it bends and zigzags across the Pacific Ocean to keep countries and island groups on a single, consistent date. That bend is exactly why it can already be January 1 on a remote Pacific island while the US is still finishing out the morning of December 31.


Kiribati itself is a great example of how this plays out. The country includes both Kiritimati, which sits on the early side of the date line, and Tarawa, which sits two hours behind it. Both places belong to the same nation, yet Tarawa reaches midnight a full two hours after Kiritimati does.


New Zealand’s Chatham Islands offer a similar, smaller-scale example. These islands run 45 minutes ahead of mainland New Zealand. During the New Year period, daylight saving time places the Chatham Islands at UTC+13:45, while Auckland and Wellington sit at UTC+13, according to New Zealand’s official daylight time order. That 45-minute gap is why Chatham Islanders get a head start on their own countrymen.


## What are the last places to enter 2027?


While Kiribati celebrates first, American Samoa and Niue are among the very last inhabited places to leave 2026 behind. Both sit at UTC−11, meaning they don’t reach midnight until a full 25 hours after Kiritimati does. That creates one of the more striking quirks of the calendar: Samoa and American Samoa, despite sharing a name and a Pacific location, ring in 2027 a full 24 hours apart because they fall on opposite sides of the International Date Line.


The very last time zone on Earth belongs to[Baker Island and Howland Island](https://www.pacioos.hawaii.edu/education/region-howlandbaker/) , two uninhabited US territories sitting at UTC−12. Once these islands finally reach midnight, the entire worldwide New Year’s rollover—from the first celebration in Kiribati to the last tick of the clock—spans a full 26 hours.


## FAQs about New Year 2027 around the world


### What time does New Zealand ring in 2027 in the US?


New Zealand’s Chatham Islands reach midnight at 5:15 a.m. ET and 2:15 a.m. PT on December 31. Auckland and Wellington follow at 6:00 a.m. ET and 3:00 a.m. PT, also on December 31.


### Who celebrates New Year first, Australia or New Zealand?


New Zealand celebrates first. Auckland reaches midnight two hours before Sydney does—6 a.m. ET compared to 8 a.m. ET on December 31.


### Why do Samoa and American Samoa celebrate a day apart?


Samoa and American Samoa sit on opposite sides of the International Date Line, even though they’re geographically close. Apia, Samoa, reaches midnight at 6 a.m. ET on December 31, while Pago Pago, American Samoa, doesn’t reach midnight until 6 a.m. ET on January 1—a full 24 hours later.


### How are these times calculated?


Each time in the table was converted from the local midnight of January 1, 2027, in that location, based on the time zones and daylight saving rules in effect during the 2026–2027 rollover.


## Mark your calendar for the people who matter


**Whether you’re tracking the countdown out of curiosity or hoping to catch a loved one the moment their New Year begins, knowing the time difference makes all the difference. Before December 31 arrives, take a moment to look up the city where your family or friends live and plan your call or message accordingly—there’s nothing like being one of the first voices they hear in 2027.**
